statements.title: thm:new:prescribed-factor
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}\label{thm:new:prescribed-factor}
For every \(\alpha>0\), there exists \(n_0=n_0(\alpha)\) such
that the following holds for every nonempty \(\mathcal S\subseteq\{3,4,\ldots\}\) and every \(n\ge n_0\).
Let $D \in 2 \mathbb{N}$ with $D\ge(\delta_{\mathcal S}+\alpha)n$.
Let \(F_1,\ldots,F_{D/2}\) be \(n\)-vertex \(2\)-regular graphs
whose connected components have lengths in \(\mathcal S\), and
let \(G\) be an \(n\)-vertex \(D\)-regular graph.
Then \(G\) has an edge-decomposition into \(F_1,\ldots,F_{D/2}\).
\end{theorem}

statements.label: cor:new:factor-consequences
statements.title: cor:new:factor-consequences
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}\label{cor:new:factor-consequences}
For every \(\alpha>0\), there exists \(n_0=n_0(\alpha)\) such
that the following holds for every odd integer \(L\ge3\) and
every \(n\ge n_0\).
Let \(F\) be an \(n\)-vertex \(2\)-factor, and let \(G\)
be a \(D\)-regular graph on \(n\) vertices, where \(D\) is even.
Then \(G\) has an \(F\)-decomposition in each of the following cases.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Every cycle of \(F\) has length at least \(L\), and
\(D\ge(1/2 + 1/(2L-2)+\alpha)n\).
\item Every cycle of \(F\) has even length, and
\(D\ge(2/3+\alpha)n\).
\item Every cycle of \(F\) has even length at least six, and
\(D\ge(1/2+\alpha)n\).
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{conjecture}\label{conj:odd_cyclic_threshold}
Let $\ell \ge3$ be an odd integer, and let $n \geq 1$ be an integer.
Let $G$ be a locally balanced $\ell$-cyclic graph with specified classes
$V_0,\ldots,V_{\ell-1}$ of size $n$. 
If $\delta_{\rm cyc}(G)\ge q_\ell n = (1/2 + 1/(2\ell-2))n$, then there is a fractional part-respecting $C_\ell$-decomposition
$\omega:\mathcal C^{\rm part}_\ell(G)\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ of $G$.
\end{conjecture}

statements.label: def:new:permutation-intervals
statements.title: Permutation distance and intervals
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Permutation distance and intervals]
\label{def:new:permutation-intervals}
Let $b\ge0$ be an integer, let $V$ be finite, and let $\pi:V\to V$
be a permutation. The \emph{$\pi$-distance} between $x,y\in V$ is
\[
 \operatorname{dist}_\pi(x,y)=\min\{|k|:k\in\mathbb Z,\ \pi^k(x)=y\},
 \qquad\min\varnothing=\infty.
\]
A set $S\subseteq V$ is \emph{$(b,\pi)$-separated} if
$\operatorname{dist}_\pi(x,y)>b$ for all distinct $x,y\in S$.
A tuple is $(b,\pi)$-separated if its entries are distinct and its entry set
is $(b,\pi)$-separated. Sets $S,T\subseteq V$ are $(b,\pi)$-separated
from each other if $\operatorname{dist}_\pi(x,y)>b$ for every $(x,y)\in S\times T$.
For $a\in V$ and a positive integer $m$ smaller than the length of its $\pi$-cycle,
put $I=\{\pi^t(a):0\le t<m\}$, $I^+=\pi^m(a)$ and $\widehat I=I\cup\{I^+\}$.
A family $\mathcal I$ of such intervals satisfies successor-extended disjointness when
\begin{equation}
 \widehat I\cap\widehat J=\varnothing\qquad(I,J\in\mathcal I,\ I\ne J).
 \label{eq:interval:extended-disjointness}
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

statements.label: def:typed-graph
statements.title: Typed graphs and physical images
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Typed graphs and physical images]
\label{def:typed-graph}
Let $V,U$ be disjoint finite sets, let $\pi:V\to V$ be a permutation,
let $R$ be a directed multigraph on $V$ whose arcs have types $0,K$,
and let $H$ be a bipartite graph with parts $V,U$ whose edges have types $0,K$.
Write $R^0,R^K$ and $H^0,H^K$ for their respective type classes.
We call $\mathcal Q=(R^0,R^K,H^0,H^K)$ a \emph{typed graph}
on $(V,U,\pi)$.
The symbol $K$ is an edge-type label with no numerical value.
For an arc occurrence $e=(x\to y,j)$, its ordered physical image is
\[
 \operatorname{phys}^{\to}(e)=
 \begin{cases}(x,y),&j=0,\\(x,\pi(y)),&j=K.\end{cases}
\]
The unordered physical image of an arc or spoke occurrence is
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{phys}(e)=\begin{cases}
 \{x,y\},&e=(x\to y,0)\in E(R^0),\\
 \{x,\pi(y)\},&e=(x\to y,K)\in E(R^K),\\
 \{x,u\},&e=(xu,j)\in E(H^j),\ j\in\{0,K\}.
 \end{cases}
 \label{eq:physical:image-map}
\end{equation}
Thus $\operatorname{phys}^{\to}:E(R)\to V\times V$ retains direction,
whereas $\operatorname{phys}:E(R)\dot\cup E(H)\to2^{V\cup U}$ forgets it.
A marked arc $x\to y$ represents the arc $x\to\pi(y)$.
For an untyped edge or arc with endpoints $x,y$, put
$\operatorname{phys}(e)=\{x,y\}$. Apply either map to a set of
occurrences by taking its image set. These formulas also apply to
potential occurrences, whether or not they belong to the host.
A family $\mathcal E$ of such arc copies is \emph{physically
injective} if $\operatorname{phys}|_{\mathcal E}$ is injective. This prevents using
two directions or types of the same physical edge. We call
$\mathcal Q$ physically injective when its rim arc family is physically
injective; this imposes no additional separation condition. Distinct physical
edges may have identical auxiliary endpoints; their arc identifiers
remain distinct. When types are fixed on physical edges before
representation, this assignment is retained by $\operatorname{phys}$.
\end{definition}

statements.label: thm:prelim:bounded-differences
statements.title: Bounded differences
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Bounded differences]
\label{thm:prelim:bounded-differences}
Let $m\ge0$ be an integer, let $t>0$, and let $b_1,\ldots,b_m\ge0$.
Let $\mathcal X_1,\ldots,\mathcal X_m$ be finite nonempty sets,
let $\xi_i$ be independent random variables taking values in $\mathcal X_i$,
and let $f:\prod_{i=1}^m\mathcal X_i\to\mathbb R$ be a function.
Put $X=f(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_m)$.
Suppose $|f(x)-f(y)|\le b_i$ whenever $x,y$ differ only in coordinate $i$.
If $\sum_{i=1}^m b_i^2>0$, then
\[
 \Pr(|X-\mathbb EX|\ge t)
 \le2\exp\left(-\frac{2t^2}{\sum_{i=1}^m b_i^2}\right).
\]
If all $b_i$ are zero, $X$ is constant.
\end{theorem}

statements.label: lem:prelim:chernoff
statements.title: Chernoff bounds
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Chernoff bounds]
\label{lem:prelim:chernoff}
Let $m\ge0$ be an integer, and let $0<\varepsilon\le1$.
Let $X_1,\ldots,X_m$ be independent random variables in $[0,1]$,
and put $X=\sum_{i=1}^mX_i$ and $\mu=\mathbb EX$.
If $\mu>0$, then
\[
 \Pr(|X-\mu|\ge\varepsilon\mu)\le2\exp(-\varepsilon^2\mu/3),
 \qquad
 \Pr(X\ge t)\le(e\mu/t)^t\quad(t\ge\mu).
\]
The same bounds hold when $V$ is a finite set, $A\subseteq V$,
$0\le r\le|V|$ is an integer, $S$ is a uniform random $r$-subset
of $V$, and $X=|S\cap A|$.
If $\mu=0$, $X=0$ almost surely.
\end{lemma}

statements.label: lem:simp:product-sampling
statements.title: Concentration for independent samples and partitions
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Concentration for independent samples and partitions]
\label{lem:simp:product-sampling}
Let $m\ge0$ be an integer, let $t>0$, and let $b_1,\ldots,b_m\ge0$.
For every $i\in[m]$, let $S_i$ be a finite set of size $D_i$, and
let $\Omega_i$ be either $\binom{S_i}{r_i}$, where $0\le r_i\le D_i$,
or the set of ordered partitions $(C_1,\ldots,C_{m_i})$ of $S_i$
with $|C_j|=n_{i,j}$, where $n_{i,j}$ are nonnegative integers
summing to $D_i$. Let $X_i$ be independent uniform random elements
of $\Omega_i$, and let $f:\prod_i\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$.
Suppose one exchange in coordinate $i$ changes $f$ by at most $b_i$.
Put $s_i=\min\{r_i,D_i-r_i\}$ in the subset case and $s_i=D_i$
in the partition case, and put $V=\sum_i s_i b_i^2$.
If $V>0$, then
\[
 \Pr\bigl(|f(X_1,\ldots,X_m)-\mathbb Ef(X_1,\ldots,X_m)|\ge t\bigr)
 \le2\exp(-2t^2/V),
\]
and each one-sided tail is at most $\exp(-2t^2/V)$.
If $V=0$, $f$ is constant on $\prod_i\Omega_i$.
\end{lemma}

statements.label: thm:prelim:max-flow-min-cut
statements.title: Max-flow/min-cut and integrality, Ford--Fulkerson~{\cite{FordFulkerson1956,FordFulkerson1957}}
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Max-flow/min-cut and integrality, Ford--Fulkerson~{\cite{FordFulkerson1956,FordFulkerson1957}}]
\label{thm:prelim:max-flow-min-cut}
Let $D$ be a finite directed graph with distinct vertices $s,t$ and
capacities $c:E(D)\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$. The maximum value of an
$s$--$t$ flow equals
\[
 \min_{\substack{S\subseteq V(D)\\s\in S,\ t\notin S}}
 \sum_{\substack{xy\in E(D)\\x\in S,\ y\notin S}}c(xy).
\]
If $c$ is integer-valued, a maximum flow can be chosen integer-valued
on every arc.
\end{theorem}

statements.label: lem:prelim:prescribed-degrees
statements.title: Prescribed degrees in a bipartite graph
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Prescribed degrees in a bipartite graph]
\label{lem:prelim:prescribed-degrees}
Let $B$ be a bipartite graph with parts $X,Y$, and let
$f:X\dot\cup Y\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ satisfy $f(X)=f(Y)$.
There is a function $q:E(B)\to[0,1]$ satisfying
$\sum_{e\in E_B(v)}q(e)=f(v)$ for every $v\in X\dot\cup Y$ if and only if
\[
 f(S)-f(Y\setminus T)\le e_B(S,T)
 \qquad(S\subseteq X,\ T\subseteq Y).
\]
If $f$ is integer-valued, $q$ can be chosen in $\{0,1\}$;
equivalently, there is a spanning subgraph $B'\subseteq B$ with
$d_{B'}(v)=f(v)$ for every $v\in X\dot\cup Y$.
\end{lemma}

statements.title: K\"onig's edge-colouring theorem
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[K\"onig's edge-colouring theorem]
\label{thm:prelim:konig}
Let $B$ be a bipartite multigraph, and put $d=\Delta(B)$.
Then there are pairwise edge-disjoint matchings $M_1,\ldots,M_d$
with $E(B)=\bigcup_{i=1}^d M_i$.
If $B$ is $d$-regular and $d>0$, each $M_i$ is perfect.
\end{theorem}

statements.label: lem:pr:cut-stability
statements.title: Stability of large cuts
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Stability of large cuts]\label{lem:pr:cut-stability}
Let $0\le\delta<1/4$, $h>0$ and $b\ge0$.
Let $J$ be a bipartite graph with parts $A_1,A_2$ of sizes $a_1,a_2>0$
satisfying the $(\delta,h)$ large-cut condition.
Let $F\subseteq J$ satisfy $\Delta(F)\le b$.
If $h'=h-b/\min\{a_1,a_2\}>0$, then $J-F$ satisfies the
$(\delta,h')$ large-cut condition.
Every bipartite graph $J'\supseteq J$ on the same parts satisfies
the $(\delta,h)$ large-cut condition.
\end{lemma}

statements.label: lem:prelim:normalized-demands
statements.title: Near-uniform demands from normalized cut estimates
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Near-uniform demands from normalized cut estimates]
\label{lem:prelim:normalized-demands}
Let $h>0$, $0\le\delta\le\delta_0<1/4$ and $M\ge0$.
Let $B$ be a bipartite graph with parts $X,Y$ of sizes $a,b>0$,
where $M\le hab/2$, and suppose
\[
 e_B(S,T)\ge hab\min\{|S|/a,|T|/b\}
 \quad(S\subseteq X,\ T\subseteq Y,\ |S|/a+|T|/b>1-2\delta_0).
\]
Let $f:X\dot\cup Y\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ satisfy $f(X)=f(Y)=M$ and
\[
 f(x)\in(1\pm\delta)M/a\quad(x\in X),\qquad
 f(y)\in(1\pm\delta)M/b\quad(y\in Y).
\]
Then there is $q:E(B)\to[0,1]$ with
$\sum_{e\in E_B(v)}q(e)=f(v)$ for every $v\in X\dot\cup Y$.
If $f$ is integer-valued, $q$ can be chosen in $\{0,1\}$.
\end{lemma}

statements.label: thm:prelim:separation
statements.title: Finite-dimensional separation
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Finite-dimensional separation]
\label{thm:prelim:separation}
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space,
let $C\subseteq E$ be nonempty, closed and convex, and let $z\in E\setminus C$.
Then there are $x\in E$ and $b\in\mathbb R$ such that
\[
 \langle x,y\rangle\le b<\langle x,z\rangle\qquad(y\in C).
\]
Consequently, for every $z\in E$, $z\in C$ if and only if
$\langle x,z\rangle\le\sup_{y\in C}\langle x,y\rangle$ for every $x\in E$.
\end{theorem}

statements.label: thm:prelim:caratheodory
statements.title: Carath\'eodory's theorem
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Carath\'eodory's theorem]
\label{thm:prelim:caratheodory}
Let $D$ be a nonnegative integer, let $X\subseteq\mathbb R^D$,
and let $z\in\operatorname{conv}(X)$.
Then there are $m\le D+1$ points $x_1,\ldots,x_m\in X$ and
$a_1,\ldots,a_m\ge0$ with $\sum_i a_i=1$ and $z=\sum_i a_ix_i$.
\end{theorem}

statements.label: thm:prelim:weighted-matching
statements.title: Ehard--Glock--Joos
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Ehard--Glock--Joos]
\label{thm:prelim:weighted-matching}
Let $k\ge2$ be an integer, let $0<d<1$, and put $a=d/(50k^2)$.
There is $\Delta_0=\Delta_0(k,d)$ such that the following holds for every $\Delta\ge\Delta_0$.
Let $\mathcal H$ be a simple $k$-uniform hypergraph with
$\Delta(\mathcal H)\le\Delta$, $\Delta_2(\mathcal H)\le\Delta^{1-d}$,
and $|E(\mathcal H)|\le\exp(\Delta^{a^2})$.
Let $\mathcal F$ be a family of at most $\exp(\Delta^{a^2})$
functions $f:E(\mathcal H)\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ satisfying
$f(E(\mathcal H))\ge\|f\|_\infty\Delta^{1+d}$.
Then there is a matching $M\subseteq E(\mathcal H)$ such that
\[
 f(M)=(1\pm\Delta^{-a})f(E(\mathcal H))/\Delta\qquad(f\in\mathcal F).
\]
\end{theorem}

statements.label: lem:new:weighted-resource-matching
statements.title: Rounding weights with prescribed local estimates
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Rounding weights with prescribed local estimates]
\label{lem:new:weighted-resource-matching}
Let $r\ge2$ and $B\ge1$ be integers, and let $K,a,\gamma>0$.
There exist $\eta_0>0$ and $n_0$, depending only on $r,B,K,a,\gamma$,
such that the following holds for every $n\ge n_0$.
Let $\mathcal H$ be a hypergraph with $|V(\mathcal H)|\le n^B$
and $2\le|\iota_{\mathcal H}(h)|\le r$ for every $h\in E(\mathcal H)$.
Let $w:E(\mathcal H)\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ satisfy
\[
 1-\eta_0\le d_w(v)\le1+\eta_0\quad(v\in V(\mathcal H)),\qquad
 d_w(u,v)\le K/n\quad(u\ne v).
\]
Let $\mathcal S\subseteq2^{V(\mathcal H)}$ have size at most $n^B$,
with $an\le|S|\le n^B$ for every $S\in\mathcal S$.
Let $\mathcal F$ be a family of at most $n^B$ functions
$g:E(\mathcal H)\to[0,1]$, and put
$W_g=\sum_{h\in E(\mathcal H)}g(h)w(h)$; suppose $W_g\ge an$ for every $g\in\mathcal F$.
Then there is a matching $M\subseteq E(\mathcal H)$ such that
\[
 |S\setminus V(M)|\le\gamma|S|\quad(S\in\mathcal S),\qquad
 g(M)\in(1\pm\gamma)W_g\quad(g\in\mathcal F).
\]
\end{lemma}

statements.label: thm:common:cycle-factor
statements.title: Cycle factors; K\"uhn--Osthus
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Cycle factors; K\"uhn--Osthus]
\label{thm:common:cycle-factor}
For every integer $r\ge3$ and every $\beta>0$, there is
$n_0=n_0(r,\beta)$ such that the following holds. Let $Q$ be
an $n$-vertex graph with $n\ge n_0$, $r\mid n$, and
\[
 \delta(Q)\ge(\mu_r+\beta)n,
 \qquad
 \mu_r=\begin{cases}
  1/2,&r\text{ even},\\
  1/2+1/(2r),&r\text{ odd}.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then $Q$ contains a $C_r$-factor.
\end{theorem}

statements.label: lem:common:fixed-length-path
statements.title: Paths of a prescribed fixed length
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Paths of a prescribed fixed length]
\label{lem:common:fixed-length-path}
Let $\beta>0$ and let $k\ge2$ and $b\ge0$ be integers.
There is $n_0=n_0(\beta,k,b)$ such that the following holds for every $n\ge n_0$.
Let $Q$ be a graph with $|V(Q)|\le n$ and $\delta(Q)\ge(1/2+\beta)n$.
Let $x,y\in V(Q)$ be distinct, and let
$S\subseteq V(Q)\setminus\{x,y\}$ satisfy $|S|\le b$.
Then there is an $x$--$y$ path $P\subseteq Q$ of length $k$
with $(V(P)\setminus\{x,y\})\cap S=\varnothing$.
\end{lemma}

statements.label: prop:family:ordinary-preparation
statements.title: Ordinary preparation
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Ordinary preparation]
\label{prop:family:ordinary-preparation}
Let $\vartheta\in[1/2,1)$, $\alpha_0,\epsilon_{\max}>0$,
$0<\varrho_*,\beta\le1$, and let $r_*\ge3$ be an integer.
There is $\xi>0$ such that, for every $\chi\in(0,1)$, there
are integers $B_{\rm abs},n_0\ge1$ with the following property.

Let $P$ be a simple $D$-regular graph on $V$, where $|V|=n\ge n_0$,
$D$ is even and $D\ge(\vartheta+\alpha_0)n$.
Let $U$ be disjoint from $V$, with $\varrho=2|U|/D\in[\varrho_*,1]$.
For each $w\in U$, let $F_w$ be an $n$-vertex two-factor whose
component lengths $r$ satisfy $\delta_{C_r}\le\vartheta$, and suppose
\[
 r_*|\{C\in\operatorname{Comp}(F_w):|C|=r_*\}|\ge\beta n
 \qquad(w\in U).
\]

Then there exists $I\subseteq V$, $|I|\le\epsilon_{\max}n$, such that the
following holds. Let $S^0$ be obtained by retaining each edge of $P$
independently with probability $\varrho$.
With probability at least $1-\chi-n^{-10}$, there is
$A\subseteq E(S^0)$, $|A|\le B_{\rm abs}$, such that every
$2|U|$-regular graph $S\subseteq P$ satisfying
\[
 \Delta(S\triangle S^0)\le\xi n,\qquad
 S[I]=S^0[I],\qquad A\subseteq E(S)
\]
has an edge-decomposition $(F'_w)_{w\in U}$ with $F'_w\cong F_w$.
\end{proposition}

statements.label: prop:family:long-preparation
statements.title: Long-cycle preparation
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Long-cycle preparation]
\label{prop:family:long-preparation}
Let $\vartheta\in[1/2,1)$, $\alpha_0,\epsilon_{\max}>0$ and
$0<\varrho_*\le1$. There are an integer $K\ge3$ and $\xi>0$
such that, for every $\chi\in(0,1)$, there are integers
$B_{\rm abs},n_0\ge1$ with the following property.

Let $P$ be a simple $D$-regular graph on $V$, where $|V|=n\ge n_0$,
$D$ is even and $D\ge(\vartheta+\alpha_0)n$.
Let $U$ be disjoint from $V$, with $\varrho=2|U|/D\in[\varrho_*,1]$.
For each $w\in U$, let $F_w$ be an $n$-vertex two-factor whose
component lengths $r$ satisfy $\delta_{C_r}\le\vartheta$, and suppose
\[
 \sum_{C\in\operatorname{Comp}(F_w):|C|>K}|C|\ge n/2
 \qquad(w\in U).
\]

Then there exists $I\subseteq V$, $|I|\le\epsilon_{\max}n$, such that the
following holds. Let $S^0$ be obtained by retaining each edge of $P$
independently with probability $\varrho$.
With probability at least $1-\chi-n^{-10}$, there is
$A\subseteq E(S^0)$, $|A|\le B_{\rm abs}$, such that every
$2|U|$-regular graph $S\subseteq P$ satisfying
\[
 \Delta(S\triangle S^0)\le\xi n,\qquad
 S[I]=S^0[I],\qquad A\subseteq E(S)
\]
has an edge-decomposition $(F'_w)_{w\in U}$ with $F'_w\cong F_w$.
\end{proposition}

statements.label: lem:family:single-copy
statements.title: One prescribed spanning factor
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[One prescribed spanning factor]
\label{lem:family:single-copy}
Fix \(\vartheta\in[1/2,1)\) and \(\alpha>0\). There is $n_0=n_0(\vartheta,\alpha)$
such that the following holds for every \(n\ge n_0\). Let \(G\)
be a simple \(D\)-regular graph on \(n\) vertices, where \(D\) is
even and \(D\ge(\vartheta+\alpha)n\). Let \(F\) be an
\(n\)-vertex \(2\)-factor such that every component length \(r\)
of \(F\) satisfies \(\delta_{C_r}\le\vartheta\). Then there is a spanning subgraph $F'\subseteq G$ with $F'\cong F$.
\end{lemma}

statements.label: lem:family:partition
statements.title: Protected regular edge partition
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Protected regular edge partition]
\label{lem:family:partition}
Fix \(\alpha>0\), a positive integer \(k\), positive lower
bounds \(\underline\varrho_a\), and positive errors \(\xi_a\),
for \(1\le a\le k\). Put $\epsilon_\Sigma=\alpha/10^5$. Let $B_0\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$
be fixed. There is
$n_0=n_0(\alpha,k,(\underline\varrho_a)_a,(\xi_a)_a,B_0)$
such that the following holds for every $n\ge n_0$.

Let \(P\) be an even \(D\)-regular simple \(n\)-vertex graph
with \(D\ge(1/2+\alpha)n\). Let \(m_a\) be positive integers,
with
\[
 \sum_a m_a=D/2,\qquad \varrho_a=2m_a/D\ge\underline\varrho_a.
\]

Let $I_a\subseteq V(P)$ be fixed sets with \(\sum_a|I_a|\le\epsilon_\Sigma n\).
Independently colour each physical edge of \(P\) with colour \(a\)
with probability \(\varrho_a\), giving graphs \(S_a^0\).

With probability at least $1-n^{-10}$, the following holds for every subsequently
specified family \(A_a\subseteq E(S_a^0)\) with $\sum_a|A_a|\le B_0$. There is a partition
\(E(P)=\dot\bigcup_a E(S_a)\) such that
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
 d_{S_a}(v)=2m_a\quad(a\in[k],\ v\in V(P)),\\
 \Delta(S_a\triangle S_a^0)\le\xi_an,\qquad A_a\subseteq E(S_a)
          \quad(a\in[k]),\\
 S_a[I_b]=S_a^0[I_b]\quad(a,b\in[k]).
\end{gathered}
\label{eq:family:partition-output}
\end{equation}

\end{lemma}

statements.label: thm:family:fixed-set
statements.title: A fixed set of allowed lengths
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[A fixed set of allowed lengths]
\label{thm:family:fixed-set}
Let \(\mathcal S\subseteq\{3,4,\ldots\}\) be nonempty and
let \(\alpha>0\). There exists \(n_0=n_0(\mathcal S,\alpha)\)
such that the following holds for every \(n\ge n_0\).
Let \(D\) be an even integer with
\(D\ge(\delta_{\mathcal S}+\alpha)n\), and let \(G\) be an
\(n\)-vertex \(D\)-regular graph. For every list
\(F_1,\ldots,F_{D/2}\) of \(n\)-vertex \(2\)-regular graphs
whose component lengths belong to \(\mathcal S\), the graph
\(G\) has an edge-decomposition into \(F_1,\ldots,F_{D/2}\).
\end{theorem}

statements.label: thm:four:two-regular-fractional-threshold
statements.title: Fractional threshold for $2$-regular graphs
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Fractional threshold for $2$-regular graphs]
\label{thm:four:two-regular-fractional-threshold}
Let $F$ be a fixed $2$-regular graph. Then
\[
  \delta_F^*\le \max\{\delta_F,1/2\}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Delcourt--Henderson--Lesgourgues--Postle
  {\cite[Theorem~2.12]{DelcourtHendersonLesgourguesPostle2025}}]
\label{thm:four:DHLP-balanced}
Let $0<\varepsilon<1$, and let $F$ be a graph with at least one edge.
There exist $\sigma,C>0$ and $n_0$, depending only on $F,\varepsilon$,
such that the following holds for every $n\ge n_0$.
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph with $\delta(G)\ge(\delta_F^*+\varepsilon)n$.
Then there is a fractional $F$-decomposition $\varphi$ of $G$ such that
\[
 \frac{\sigma}{\binom{n-2}{v(F)-2}}
 \le\varphi(F')\le\frac{C}{\binom{n-2}{v(F)-2}}
 \qquad(F'\cong F,\ F'\subseteq G).
\]
\end{theorem}

statements.label: thm:four:dense-spread
statements.title: Positive bounded fractional $C_\ell$-decomposition
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Positive bounded fractional $C_\ell$-decomposition]
\label{thm:four:dense-spread}
Let $\ell\ge3$ be an integer, and let $\alpha>0$.
There exist $c,C>0$ and $n_0$, depending only on $\ell,\alpha$,
such that the following holds for every $n\ge n_0$.
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph with $\delta(G)\ge(\delta_{C_\ell}+\alpha)n$.
Then there is a fractional $C_\ell$-decomposition $\omega$ of $G$ with
\[
 cn^{2-\ell}\le\omega(C')\le Cn^{2-\ell}
 \qquad(C'\in\mathcal C_\ell(G)).
\]
For all distinct $e,f\in E(G)$, it also satisfies
\[
 L_\omega^E(e,f):=\sum_{\substack{C'\in\mathcal C_\ell(G)\\e,f\in E(C')}}\omega(C')
 \le\begin{cases}C/n,&e,f\text{ share a vertex},\\
                 C/n^2,&e,f\text{ are disjoint}.
     \end{cases}
\]
\end{theorem}

statements.label: lem:four:wheel-rounding
statements.title: Approximate $r$-wheel packings with a local leftover bound
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Approximate $r$-wheel packings with a local leftover bound]
\label{lem:four:wheel-rounding}
Let $r\ge3$ be an integer, and let $C,C_V,\gamma>0$.
There is $n_0=n_0(r,C,C_V,\gamma)$ such that the following holds for every $n\ge n_0$.
Let $\mathcal G=(V,U,G,H)$ be an extended graph with $|V|+|U|\le C_Vn$,
and let $\omega$ be a fractional $r$-wheel decomposition of $\mathcal G$
satisfying $\omega(W)\le Cn^{1-r}$ for every $W\in\mathcal W_r(\mathcal G)$.
Then there is an $r$-wheel packing $\mathcal P$ in $\mathcal G$ such that
\[
 L=\mathcal G-\bigcup_{W\in\mathcal P}W
 \qquad\text{satisfies}\qquad \Delta(L)\le\gamma n.
\]
\end{lemma}

statements.label: doLpart:lem:conditional-realization
statements.title: Conditional realization
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Conditional realization]\label{doLpart:lem:conditional-realization}
Let $k\ge2$ be an integer, and let $B>0$.
Let $X_0,\ldots,X_{k-1}$ be disjoint finite sets, indexed modulo $k$.
For every $i$, let $I_i$ be a sequence of vertex classes from $X_i$ to $X_{i+1}$
with at least one internal class; suppose all internal classes are disjoint
from each other and from the $X_j$.
Let $G$ be a graph on these classes, and let $\mathcal P_i$ be the paths in $G$
that use one vertex from each class of $I_i$ in the specified order.
Let $\lambda_i:\mathcal P_i\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ have total mass $B$, and put
\[
 K_i(x,z)=\sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_i\\\partial P=(x,z)}}\lambda_i(P)
 \qquad(x\in X_i,\ z\in X_{i+1}).
\]
Let $J:\prod_{i=0}^{k-1}X_i\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ have total mass $B$
and $(X_i,X_{i+1})$ marginal $K_i$ for every $i$.
Let $\mathcal C$ be the family of cycles formed by concatenating one path
from each $\mathcal P_i$ in cyclic class order. For $C\in\mathcal C$,
let $P_i(C)$ be its subpath through the classes of $I_i$.
Then there is $\omega:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ of total mass $B$ with
\[
 \sum_{\substack{C\in\mathcal C\\ P_i(C)=P}}\omega(C)=\lambda_i(P)
 \quad(i\in\mathbb Z/k\mathbb Z,\ P\in\mathcal P_i).
\]
\end{lemma}

statements.label: doLpart:cor:spread
statements.title: Positive bounded weights at a positive degree margin
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Positive bounded weights at a positive degree margin]
\label{doLpart:cor:spread}
Let $k\ge2$ be an integer, put $\ell=2k$ and $q=k/(2k-1)$,
and let $0<\alpha\le1-q$.
There exist $a_-,a_+>0$, depending only on $k,\alpha$, such that the following holds.
Let $n\ge1$ be an integer, and let $G$ be a locally balanced $\ell$-cyclic graph
with classes $V_0,\ldots,V_{\ell-1}$ of size $n$ and $\delta_{\rm cyc}(G)\ge(q+\alpha)n$.
Then there is a fractional part-respecting $C_\ell$-decomposition $\omega$ of $G$ with
\[
 a_-n^{2-\ell}\le\omega(C)\le a_+n^{2-\ell}\qquad(C\in\mathcal C^{\rm part}_\ell(G)).
\]
For all distinct $e,f\in E(G)$, it also satisfies
\[
 \sum_{\substack{C\in\mathcal C^{\rm part}_\ell(G)\\e,f\in E(C)}}\omega(C)
 \le\begin{cases}
 a_+n^{-1},&e,f\text{ have a common endpoint},\\
 a_+n^{-2},&e,f\text{ are vertex-disjoint}.
 \end{cases}
\]
\end{corollary}

statements.label: doLpart:thm:odd
statements.title: doLpart:thm:odd
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}\label{doLpart:thm:odd}
Let $k\ge2$ and $n\ge1$ be integers, and put $\ell=2k+1$.
Let $G$ be a locally balanced $\ell$-cyclic graph with specified
classes $V_0,\ldots,V_{\ell-1}$ of size $n$. If
\[
 \delta_{\rm cyc}(G)\ge\frac{k}{2k-1}n,
\]
then $G$ has a fractional part-respecting $C_\ell$-decomposition.
\end{theorem}

statements.label: thm:four:long-capacities
statements.title: Long cyclic-partite capacity decomposition
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Long cyclic-partite capacity decomposition]
\label{thm:four:long-capacities}
Fix $0<\kappa<1$, $B\ge1$, and positive constants
$a_-,a_+,d_-,d_+$.

Let $t$ be an integer satisfying
\[
 t\ge 1+3\left\lceil
      \frac{\log(10(B+1))}{-\log(1-\kappa)}
                                  \right\rceil .
\]

Let $c\ge12t+4$ be an integer. There exist $b_-,b_+>0$,
depending only on $\kappa,B,a_-,a_+,d_-,d_+,t,c$, such that the
following holds for every integer $n\ge1$.

Let $V_0,\ldots,V_{c-1}$ be disjoint sets of size $n$, and let
$a_i:V_i\times V_{i+1}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ be locally balanced
capacity functions. For $i\in\mathbb Z/c\mathbb Z$ and $x\in V_i$, define
\[
 d_i(x)=\sum_{y\in V_{i+1}}a_i(x,y)
       =\sum_{z\in V_{i-1}}a_{i-1}(z,x),\qquad
 M=\sum_{x\in V_i}d_i(x),
\]
where local balance makes $M$ independent of $i$.

Suppose every positive capacity lies in $[a_-,a_+]$ and
$d_-n\le d_i(x)\le d_+n$. Define
\[
 P_i(x,y)=a_i(x,y)/d_i(x),\qquad \pi_i(x)=d_i(x)/M.
\]

Let $J\subseteq\mathbb Z/c\mathbb Z$
with $|J|\le1$ index the exceptional interfaces. For $i\notin J$, $x\in V_i$ and $y\in V_{i+1}$ suppose that
\[
 P_i(x,y)\le B\pi_{i+1}(y).
\]
For each $i$ with $i,i+1,i+2\notin J$, suppose that
\[
 (P_iP_{i+1}P_{i+2})(x,y)\ge\kappa\pi_{i+3}(y)
                       \quad(x\in V_i,\ y\in V_{i+3}).
\]

Let $\mathcal C$ consist of the directed transversal cycles
$x_0x_1\cdots x_{c-1}x_0$ with $x_i\in V_i$ and
$a_i(x_i,x_{i+1})>0$ for every $i$.

Then there is $\lambda:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ satisfying
\[
 \sum_{\substack{C\in\mathcal C\\(x,y)\in E(C)}}\lambda(C)
      =a_i(x,y)
 \quad(i\in\mathbb Z/c\mathbb Z,\ x\in V_i,\ y\in V_{i+1}),
\]
and
\[
 b_-n^{2-c}\le\lambda(C)\le b_+n^{2-c}
                  \qquad(C\in\mathcal C).
\]
\end{theorem}

statements.label: lem:four:zonotope
statements.title: From approximate bounded weights to exact bounded weights
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[From approximate bounded weights to exact bounded weights]
\label{lem:four:zonotope}
Let $\kappa,B,\varepsilon>0$ with $\varepsilon<\kappa$.
Let $E$ be finite, let $S\subseteq\mathbb R^E$ be a subspace,
let $\mathcal P$ be a finite family of vectors in $S$, and let $w\in S$.
Suppose that, for every $w'\in S$ with
$\|w'-w\|_\infty\le\kappa$, there is
$\lambda_{w'}:\mathcal P\to[0,B]$ satisfying
\[
 \left\|\sum_{P\in\mathcal P}\lambda_{w'}(P)P-w'\right\|_\infty
                  \le\varepsilon.
\]
Then there is $\lambda:\mathcal P\to[0,B]$ with
$\sum_{P\in\mathcal P}\lambda(P)P=w$.
\end{lemma}

statements.label: lem:four:random-regularization
statements.title: Regularization with controlled deletion probabilities
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Regularization with controlled deletion probabilities]
\label{lem:four:random-regularization}
Fix $\beta>0$. There are $C,\eta_0>0$ such that, for every
$0<\eta<\eta_0$, there is an integer $m_0$ with the following property.
Let $m\ge m_0$, let $d\in\mathbb R$, and let $B[A_1,A_2]$ be
bipartite with $|A_1|=|A_2|=m$, with minimum
degree at least $(1/2+\beta)m$, and degrees in
$[d-\eta m,d+\eta m]$.
Then there is a random spanning $k$-regular subgraph $R\subseteq B$,
where $k=\lfloor d-\sqrt\eta m\rfloor$, such that
$\Pr(e\notin E(R))\le C\sqrt\eta$ for every $e\in E(B)$.
\end{lemma}

statements.label: thm:four:successor-kernel
statements.title: Successor weights with uniform positional loads
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Successor weights with uniform positional loads]
\label{thm:four:successor-kernel}
Fix an even integer $c\ge4$ and $\beta>0$;
put $q_c=c/(2c-2)$. There are $a,C>0$ such that, for every
$\tau>0$, there is $\varepsilon_0>0$ with the following property.
For every integer $b\ge2$ there is an integer $n_0$ such that the
following holds.

Let $G$ be a simple graph on $V$, $|V|=n\ge n_0$, and let
$D\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
 n/2\le D\le2n,\qquad |d_G(v)-D|\le\varepsilon_0n\quad(v\in V).
 \label{eq:near-regular:degree-errors}
\end{equation}
Suppose $\delta(G)\ge(q_c+\beta)n$. Let $\pi$ be a permutation
of $V$.
Let $\mathcal T_K$ be the family of $(b,\pi)$-separated tuples
$\mathbf x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{c-1})$ whose physical edges
\[
 x_0x_1,\ldots,x_{c-2}x_{c-1},x_{c-1}\pi(x_0)
\]
belong to $G$. Then there is $\lambda_K:\mathcal T_K\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$
such that
\[
 \sum_{\mathbf x:x_i=x,\ x_{i+1}=y}\lambda_K(\mathbf x)=1\pm\tau
 \quad(0\le i<c-1,\ xy\in E(G),\ \operatorname{dist}_\pi(x,y)>b),
\]
\[
 \sum_{\mathbf x:x_{c-1}=x,\ \pi(x_0)=y}\lambda_K(\mathbf x)=1\pm\tau
 \quad(xy\in E(G),\ \operatorname{dist}_\pi(x,\pi^{-1}(y))>b),
\]
and
\[
 \sum_{\mathbf x:x_i=v}\lambda_K(\mathbf x)=(1\pm\tau)D
 \quad(0\le i<c,\ v\in V),\qquad
 an^{2-c}\le\lambda_K(\mathbf x)\le Cn^{2-c}
 \quad(\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_K).
\]

\end{theorem}

statements.label: lem:pr:rt1-stability
statements.title: Stability of neighbourhood counts
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Stability of neighbourhood counts]
\label{lem:pr:rt1-stability}
Let $A$ be finite, let $k\ge0$ be an integer, and let $b\ge0$.
Let $N_j,N_j'\subseteq A$ for $j\in[k]$ satisfy
$|N_j\triangle N_j'|\le b$. Put
\[
 Z=\left|\bigcap_{j\in[k]}N_j\right|,\qquad
 Z'=\left|\bigcap_{j\in[k]}N_j'\right|,
\]
where an empty intersection is $A$. Then $|Z'-Z|\le kb$.
If $\mu\in\mathbb R$, $e\ge0$, $|Z-\mu|\le e$ and $D\subseteq A$, then
\[
 |Z'-\mu|\le e+kb,\qquad
 \left|(A\setminus D)\cap\bigcap_{j\in[k]}N_j'\right|
 \ge\mu-e-kb-|D|.
\]
\end{lemma}

statements.label: cor:cn:relative-typicality-large-cuts
statements.title: Large cuts from relative neighbourhood estimates
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Large cuts from relative neighbourhood estimates]
\label{cor:cn:relative-typicality-large-cuts}
Let $0<\alpha<1/2$, $p_*>0$, $0<\nu\le1$, $\eta,f\ge0$,
and $0<\delta\le\min\{\alpha/4,\nu/8\}$. Let
$G[A_1,A_2]$ be bipartite, $J\subseteq G$, $F_1$ a graph on $A_1$
with $\Delta(F_1)\le f$, and $p_x\in[p_*,1]$ for $x\in A_1$.

Put $a=|A_1|>0$, $b=|A_2|>0$. Suppose that, for every ordered pair $x\ne x'$ with
$xx'\notin E(F_1)$,
\begin{align}
 |N_J(x)\cap N_J(x')|&\le p_xp_{x'}|N_G(x)\cap N_G(x')|+\eta b,\notag\\
 |N_J(x)\cap N_G(x')|&\ge p_x|N_G(x)\cap N_G(x')|-\eta b.
 \label{eq:cn:relative-cut-input}
\end{align}

Suppose
\[
 d_G(x)\ge(1/2+\alpha)b,\quad d_J(x)\ge\nu b\quad(x\in A_1),
\]
\[
 d_G(z)\ge(1/2+\alpha)a,\quad d_J(z)\ge\nu a\quad(z\in A_2).
\]
If
\[
 \sqrt{12\eta/\nu+16(f+1)/(\nu^2a)}\le p_*\alpha/4,
\]
then $J$ satisfies the large-cut condition
\eqref{eq:cuts:large} with parameters $\delta,h_0$, where
$h_0=\tfrac12\min\{\nu,p_*\alpha\}$.
\end{corollary}

statements.label: def:four:local-interval-law
statements.title: Raw interval sample
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Raw interval sample]\label{def:four:local-interval-law}
Choose mutually independent variables
$A_{w,a}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(a_d)$ and $G_{w,a}$,
for $(w,a)\in W\times V$, with
\[
 \Pr(G_{w,a}=g)=q_g(w)/(dr_d)\quad(g\in\Gamma),\qquad
 \Pr(G_{w,a}=\bot)=1-Q(w)/(dr_d).
\]
Independently of these variables, choose independent $B_{w,x}$ with
\[
 \Pr(B_{w,x}=j)=s_j(w)/\overline q(w)\quad(j\in\Sigma),\qquad
 \Pr(B_{w,x}=\bot)=1-\sum_j s_j(w)/\overline q(w).
\]
For each $w\in W$, put
\[
 K_w=\{a\in V:A_{w,a}=1,\ A_{w,b}=0
       \text{ for every }b\ne a\text{ with }\operatorname{dist}_\pi(a,b)\le d\}.
\]
Define
\[
 \mathcal X_w^g=\{I_a:a\in K_w,\ G_{w,a}=g\}.
\]
The families $\mathcal X$, together with $B$, form the
\emph{raw interval sample} with parameters $(q_g),(s_j)$.
\end{definition}

statements.label: lem:interval:raw-law
statements.title: Raw marginals and independence
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Raw marginals and independence]\label{lem:interval:raw-law}
For a raw interval sample and every $w\in W$, $x\in V$,
\[
 \Pr(x\in X_w^g)=q_g(w),\qquad
 \Pr(x\in\overline X_w)=\overline q(w),\qquad
 \Pr(\sigma_{\mathcal X}(xw)=j)=s_j(w)
 \quad(g\in\Gamma,\ j\in\Sigma).
\]
For every $(3d,\pi)$-separated $S\subseteq V$, the raw states
$(\sigma_{\mathcal X}(xw))_{x\in S}$ are independent.
The vectors $(\sigma_{\mathcal X}(xw))_{x\in V}$ are independent
as $w$ varies.
\end{lemma}

statements.label: def:interval:retention
statements.title: Uniform retention
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Uniform retention]\label{def:interval:retention}
Fix $\Gamma_{\rm trim}\subseteq\Gamma$. For $g\in\Gamma_{\rm trim}$ put
\[
 N_a^g=|\{w:I_a\in\mathcal X_w^g\}|,\qquad t_g=\min_{a\in V}N_a^g.
\]
Fix the values of $(A_{w,a}),(G_{w,a}),(B_{w,x})$.
Independently for each $(a,g)$, choose a uniform $t_g$-subset
$J_{a,g}$ of $\{w:I_a\in\mathcal X_w^g\}$. Set
\[
 \mathcal Y_w^g=\{I_a:w\in J_{a,g}\}\quad(g\in\Gamma_{\rm trim}),
 \qquad \mathcal Y_w^g=\mathcal X_w^g\quad(g\notin\Gamma_{\rm trim}).
\]
The retained assignment is $\sigma_{\mathcal Y}$ in
\eqref{eq:interval:assignment}, using the same $B$.
\end{definition}

statements.label: lem:pr:rt1-realisation
statements.title: Ordinary neighbourhood counts
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Ordinary neighbourhood counts]
\label{lem:pr:rt1-realisation}
Fix integers $h\ge0$ and $d\ge2$. There is $c_{h,d}>0$ such that
the following holds for every $\varepsilon>0$.
Let $V,U$ be finite disjoint sets, let $P$ be a graph on $V$, and let
$\pi$ be a permutation of $V$ with $L_\pi>10d$.
Let $F$ be a graph on $V$ containing every distinct pair at $\pi$-distance at most $3d$,
and let $P_{\rm el}\subseteq P$ and $q\in[0,1]$.
Let $\sigma_{\mathcal X}$ be the raw assignment of a local interval
sample on $(V,U,\pi)$ with parameter $d$ and functions
$q_1,q_2,(\widetilde s_j)_{j\in\mathcal J}$, and fix $j_0\in\mathcal J$.
Put $s=\widetilde s_{j_0}$ and
\[
 E(H)=\{xu:\sigma_{\mathcal X}(xu)=j_0\}.
\]
Independently of all pair variables, retain each edge of $P_{\rm el}$
independently with probability $q$, obtaining $R$.
Let $(N_i,\mu_i,a_i)_{i\in\mathcal I}$ be a fixed ordinary
neighbourhood count family with bound $h$, with
graphs $P,P_{\rm el},F$ and sampling parameters $q,s$ as above. Then, for $\mathcal B=(R,H)$,
\[
 \mathbb E N_i(\mathcal B)=\mu_i\quad(i\in\mathcal I),\qquad
 \Pr\bigl(\exists i\in\mathcal I:
 |N_i(\mathcal B)-\mu_i|>\varepsilon a_i\bigr)
 \le\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}2e^{-c_{h,d}\varepsilon^2a_i}.
\]
\end{lemma}

statements.label: lem:pr:marked-realisation
statements.title: Marked neighbourhood counts
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Marked neighbourhood counts]
\label{lem:pr:marked-realisation}
Fix integers $h\ge0$ and $d\ge2$. There is $c_{h,d}>0$ such that
the following holds for every $\varepsilon>0$.
Let $V,U$ be finite disjoint sets, let $P$ be a graph on $V$, and let
$\pi$ be a permutation of $V$ with $L_\pi>10d$.
Let $F$ be a graph on $V$ containing every distinct pair at $\pi$-distance at most $3d$.
Let $\sigma_{\mathcal X}$ be the raw assignment of a local interval
sample on $(V,U,\pi)$ with parameter $d$ and functions
$q_1,q_2,(\widetilde s_j)_{j\in\mathcal J}$.
Fix $j_0\in\mathcal J$ and $g_0\in\{1,2\}$, and put
$s_0=\widetilde s_{j_0}$, $s_K=q_{g_0}$ and
\[
 E(H^0)=\{xu:\sigma_{\mathcal X}(xu)=j_0\},\qquad
 E(H^K)=\{xu:\sigma_{\mathcal X}(xu)=g_0\}.
\]
Let $E_0,E_K\subseteq\{(x,y):\{x,y\}\in E(P)\}$ and
$p_0,p_K\in[0,1]$. Put
$m_j(e)=|\{(x,y)\in E_j:\{x,y\}=e\}|$ and assume
\begin{equation}
 m_0(e)p_0+m_K(e)p_K\le1\quad(e\in E(P)).
 \label{eq:cn:physical-state-feasibility}
\end{equation}
If $p_K>0$, suppose $(x,\pi(x))\notin E_K$ for every $x\in V$.
Independently over physical edges and independently of all pair variables,
choose $C_e$ with probability $p_j$ at each state $(x,y,j)$ for which
$(x,y)\in E_j$ and $\{x,y\}=e$, and with the remaining mass at $\bot$.
Put
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E(R^0)&=\{x\to y:C_{\{x,y\}}=(x,y,0)\},\\
 E(R^K)&=\{x\to\pi^{-1}(y):C_{\{x,y\}}=(x,y,K)\},
 \qquad\mathcal B=(R^0,R^K,H^0,H^K).
\end{aligned}
\]
Let $(N_i,\mu_i,a_i)_{i\in\mathcal I}$ be a fixed marked
neighbourhood count family with bound $h$, with
these eligible arcs and sampling parameters. Then
\[
 \mathbb E N_i(\mathcal B)=\mu_i\quad(i\in\mathcal I),\qquad
 \Pr\bigl(\exists i\in\mathcal I:
 |N_i(\mathcal B)-\mu_i|>\varepsilon a_i\bigr)
 \le\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}2e^{-c_{h,d}\varepsilon^2a_i}.
\]
\end{lemma}

statements.label: lem:pr:wcodeg-realisation
statements.title: Realization of weighted codegrees
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Realization of weighted codegrees]
\label{lem:pr:wcodeg-realisation}
Fix $p_*>0$. There is $c_{p_*}>0$, depending only on $p_*$, such that
the following holds for every $\eta>0$ and integer $d\ge2$.
Let $V,U$ be disjoint
finite sets and let $\pi$ be a permutation of $V$ whose cycles have length
greater than $10d$. Fix $A\subseteq V$, $\varnothing\ne B\subseteq U$
and a pair-state value $a$. Let $\sigma_{\mathcal X}$ be the raw assignment
of a local interval sample on $(V,U,\pi)$ with interval length $d$.
Write
\[
 p_u=\Pr(\sigma_{\mathcal X}(vu)=a)\ge p_*\quad(u\in B),\qquad
 E(H)=\{vu:v\in A,\ u\in B,\ \sigma_{\mathcal X}(vu)=a\}.
\]
The marginal $p_u$ is independent of $v$ under the stated law.
Let $F_A$ be a fixed graph on $A$ containing every distinct pair
$\{x,y\}$ with $\operatorname{dist}_\pi(x,y)\le3d$.
Then
\[
 \Pr\left(\exists x\ne y\in A,\ xy\notin E(F_A):\
 \left|\frac1{|B|}\sum_{u\in N_H(x)\cap N_H(y)}p_u^{-2}-1\right|>\eta\right)
 \le2|A|^2\exp(-c_{p_*}\eta^2|B|).
\]
\end{lemma}

statements.label: lem:four:sparse-alternating
statements.title: Alternating corrections from intersection estimates
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Alternating corrections from intersection estimates]
\label{lem:four:sparse-alternating}
Fix $p_*>0$. There are constants $\delta_0,C>0$ with the
following property for every $\delta\ge0$ and integer $D\ge1$.

Let $H$ be bipartite with parts $A,B$ of positive sizes $a,b$, and assign a number $p_u\in[p_*,1]$ to
each $u\in B$. For $x,y\in A$, define
\[
 \kappa_H(x,y)=\sum_{u\in N_H(x)\cap N_H(y)}p_u^{-2}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $d_H(u)=(p_u\pm\delta)a$ for every $u\in B$;
\item for $k\in\{2,3\}$ and distinct $u_1,\ldots,u_k\in B$,
\[
 \left|\bigcap_{i=1}^kN_H(u_i)\right|
           =\left(\prod_{i=1}^kp_{u_i}\pm\delta\right)a;
\]
\item for each $x\in A$, there is $E_x\subseteq A$ with $|E_x|\le D$ such that every $y\in A\setminus E_x$ satisfies
\[
 \left|\kappa_H(x,y)-b\right|
       \le\delta b.
\]
\end{enumerate}

Suppose $\delta+D/a+1/b\le\delta_0$. Define
\[
 \mathcal Q_4(H)=\{(x,u,y,v):x\ne y\in A,\ u\ne v\in B,\
                                      xu,yu,yv,xv\in E(H)\},
\]
and, for $Q=(x,u,y,v)$, put
$\delta_Q=\ind_{xu}-\ind_{yu}+\ind_{yv}-\ind_{xv}\in\mathbb R^{E(H)}$.

Then, for every $z:E(H)\to\mathbb R$ satisfying
$\sum_{e\ni v}z(e)=0$ for every $v\in A\cup B$, there is
$t:\mathcal Q_4(H)\to\mathbb R$ such that
\[
 z=\sum_{Q\in\mathcal Q_4(H)}t(Q)\delta_Q,\qquad
 \sum_{Q\in\mathcal Q_4(H):Q\ni e}|t(Q)|\le C\|z\|_\infty
                  \quad(e\in E(H)).
\]
\end{lemma}

statements.label: def:ordinary-local-reference
statements.title: Ordinary completion sample
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Ordinary completion sample]
\label{def:ordinary-local-reference}
Let $P$ be a graph on $V$, let $U$ be disjoint from $V$, let $d\ge2$ be an integer,
and let $\pi$ be a permutation of $V$ with $L_\pi>10d$.
Let $0<\varrho\le1$, $0<s\le1/100$ and $a_u,b_u\ge0$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
 a_u\le1/8,\qquad
 s+b_u\le\overline q(u):=1-(1+1/d)a_u\quad(u\in U).
 \label{eq:completion:ordinary-pair-feasibility}
\end{equation}
Take a raw interval sample with interval colour $2$ and ordinary
colours $\mathrm o_1,\mathrm o_2$, using the functions
$q_2(u)=a_u$, $s_{\mathrm o_1}(u)=s$ and
$s_{\mathrm o_2}(u)=b_u$. No interval is removed: put
$\mathcal Y=\mathcal X$. Let $H^0$ be the bipartite graph on $(V,U)$ with
\[
 E(H^0)=\{xu:\sigma_{\mathcal X}(xu)=\mathrm o_1\}
       =\{xu:x\in\overline X_u,\ B_{u,x}=\mathrm o_1\}.
\]
Independently of the pair experiment, retain each edge of $P$
with probability $\varrho s$. Let $R$ contain the retained edges
$xy$ with $\operatorname{dist}_\pi(x,y)>3d$.
We call $\mathcal B=(R,H^0)$ the \emph{ordinary completion sample}
with parameters $\varrho,s,d,(a_u),(b_u)$.
When distinguishing raw and retained samples, write
$\mathcal B_{\mathcal X}=\mathcal B_{\mathcal Y}=\mathcal B$.
\end{definition}

statements.label: def:completion:marked-sample
statements.title: Marked completion sample
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Marked completion sample]
\label{def:completion:marked-sample}
Let $P$ be a graph on $V$, let $U$ be disjoint from $V$, let $d\ge2$ be an integer,
and let $\pi$ be a permutation of $V$ with $L_\pi>10d$.
Let $c\ge8$ be even, $0<\varrho\le1$, $0<s\le1/100$, and put
\begin{equation}
 t=\frac{s}{c-1},\qquad p=\frac{\varrho s}{2},\qquad
 k=\frac{\varrho t}{2}.
 \label{eq:family:marked-probabilities}
\end{equation}
Let $a_u,b_u\ge0$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
 t+a_u\le1/8,\qquad
 s+b_u\le\overline q(u):=1-(1+1/d)(t+a_u)\quad(u\in U).
 \label{eq:completion:pair-feasibility}
\end{equation}
Take a raw interval sample with interval colours $1,2$ and ordinary
colours $\mathrm o_1,\mathrm o_2$, using the functions
$q_1(u)=t$, $q_2(u)=a_u$,
$s_{\mathrm o_1}(u)=s$, $s_{\mathrm o_2}(u)=b_u$. Put
\[
 N_a^1=|\{u:I_a\in\mathcal X_u^1\}|,\qquad
 t_1=\min_{a\in V}N_a^1.
\]
Conditional on all raw variables, choose, independently for each $a\in V$,
a uniform $t_1$-subset $T_a^1$ of $\{u:I_a\in\mathcal X_u^1\}$.
Set
\[
 \mathcal Y_u^1=\{I_a:u\in T_a^1\},\qquad
 \mathcal Y_u^2=\mathcal X_u^2.
\]
Thus $T_a^1=J_{a,1}$ in the uniform-retention rule.
For $\mathcal Z\in\{\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\}$, put
\begin{equation}
 E(H^0_{\mathcal Z})=\{xu:\sigma_{\mathcal Z}(xu)=\mathrm o_1\},
 \qquad E(H^K_{\mathcal Z})=\{xu:\sigma_{\mathcal Z}(xu)=1\}.
 \label{eq:completion:selected-pairs}
\end{equation}
Both assignments use the same preassigned variables $B_{u,x}$,
including labels newly entering $\overline Y_u$.

Independently over unordered edges $e=\{x,y\}\in E(P)$, and
independently of all pair and retention variables, choose $C_e$
with probabilities $p,p,k,k$ on
$(x,y,0),(y,x,0),(x,y,K),(y,x,K)$ and the remaining mass on $\bot$.
Put
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E(R^0)&=\{x\to y:xy\in E(P),\ C_{xy}=(x,y,0),\
                         \operatorname{dist}_\pi(x,y)>3d\},\\
 E(R^K)&=\{x\to z:x\pi(z)\in E(P),\ C_{x\pi(z)}=(x,\pi(z),K),\
                         \operatorname{dist}_\pi(x,z)>3d\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
We call
$\mathcal B=\mathcal B_{\mathcal Y}
=(R^0,R^K,H^0_{\mathcal Y},H^K_{\mathcal Y})$
the \emph{marked completion sample} with parameters
$c,\varrho,s,d,(a_u),(b_u)$, and put
$\mathcal B_{\mathcal X}=(R^0,R^K,H^0_{\mathcal X},H^K_{\mathcal X})$.
\end{definition}

statements.label: lem:completion:trimming-restrictions
statements.title: Interval assignment changes on fixed restrictions
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Interval assignment changes on fixed restrictions]
\label{lem:completion:trimming-restrictions}
Fix an integer $d\ge2$ and constants
$p_{\rm trim},\zeta>0$, $C\ge1$ and $Q\ge1$.
There are integers $m_{\rm trim},n_0\ge1$ with the following property.
Let $n\ge n_0$, $|V|=n$ and $|U|\le n$, and let $\pi$ be a
permutation of $V$ with $L_\pi>10d$. Let $t,s>0$ and $a_u,b_u\ge0$.
Take a raw interval sample with interval functions $q_1(u)=t$, $q_2(u)=a_u$ and ordinary-spoke
functions $s_{\mathrm o_1}(u)=s$, $s_{\mathrm o_2}(u)=b_u$, satisfying
\eqref{eq:completion:pair-feasibility}. Assume $t|U|\ge p_{\rm trim}n$.
Apply uniform retention with $\Gamma_{\rm trim}=\{1\}$ and put $T_a^1=J_{a,1}$;
in particular, $\mathcal Y_u^2=\mathcal X_u^2$.
Let $\sigma_{\mathcal X},\sigma_{\mathcal Y}$ be the assignments
\eqref{eq:interval:assignment} before and after this retention.
Fix a family $\mathcal R$ of at most $n^C$
pairs $(S,T)$, where
$S\subseteq V$ is a union of cycles of $\pi$, $T\subseteq U$, and
\begin{equation}
 |S|,|T|\ge m_{\rm trim},\qquad C^{-1}|S|\le|T|\le C|S|.
 \label{eq:new:nested-successors:N7}
\end{equation}
Then, with probability at least $1-n^{-Q}$, simultaneously
\begin{equation}
 \left|N_a^1-\frac{t|U|}{d}\right|\le n^{3/5}
 \quad(a\in V),
 \label{eq:trimming:restriction-starts}
\end{equation}
and for every
$(S,T)\in\mathcal R$,
\[
 |\{x\in S:\sigma_{\mathcal X}(xu)\ne\sigma_{\mathcal Y}(xu)\}|
 \le\zeta|S|\quad(u\in U),
\]
\[
 |\{u\in T:\sigma_{\mathcal X}(xu)\ne\sigma_{\mathcal Y}(xu)\}|
 \le\zeta|T|\quad(x\in V).
\]
\end{lemma}

statements.label: lem:pr:wi-stability
statements.title: Changes of weighted products
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Changes of weighted products]
\label{lem:pr:wi-stability}
Let $E,\mathcal C$ be finite sets, and let each $\Sigma_e$ be a
nonempty finite set. Put $\Sigma=\prod_{e\in E}\Sigma_e$.
For $i\in\mathcal C$, let $F_i\subseteq E$,
$s_i\in\prod_{e\in F_i}\Sigma_e$ and $w_i\ge0$.
For $\rho\in\Sigma$, put
\[
 Z(\rho)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal C}w_i\prod_{e\in F_i}\ind_{\{\rho(e)=s_i(e)\}},
 \qquad b(e)=\sum_{i:e\in F_i}w_i.
\]
If $\sigma,\tau\in\Sigma$ differ only on $D\subseteq E$, then
\[
 |Z(\tau)-Z(\sigma)|\le\sum_{e\in D}b(e).
\]
\end{lemma}

statements.label: lem:pr:wi-interactions
statements.title: A sufficient incidence bound
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[A sufficient incidence bound]
\label{lem:pr:wi-interactions}
Fix $C,B\ge1$ and $a\ge1$. Let $E,J$ be finite,
let $\mathcal T$ be a finite indexed family of subsets of $E$, and
let $w_T\ge0$ for $T\in\mathcal T$. Define
\[
 \mathscr Z(\mathbf u)=\sum_{T\in\mathcal T}w_T\prod_{f\in T}u_f
       \quad(\mathbf u\in\{0,1\}^E),\qquad b(f)=\sum_{T\ni f}w_T.
\]
Let independent coordinates $\xi_j\in\mathcal Z_j$, $j\in J$,
determine indicators $I_f:\prod_{j\in J}\mathcal Z_j\to\{0,1\}$,
and put $Z(\mathbf z)=\mathscr Z((I_f(\mathbf z))_{f\in E})$.
Suppose $E_1\dot\cup E_2=\{f:b(f)>0\}$ satisfies
\[
 |E_1|\le Ca,\quad b(f)\le C/a\ (f\in E_1),\qquad
 |E_2|\le Ca^2,\quad b(f)\le C/a^2\ (f\in E_2).
\]
Assume each $I_f$ with $b(f)>0$ depends on at most $B$ coordinates,
and any change of one coordinate changes at most $B$ such indicators.

Then there are $c_j\ge0$, $j\in J$, such that
\[
 \sum_{j\in J}c_j^2\le2C^3B^3/a,\qquad
 |Z(\mathbf z)-Z(\mathbf z')|\le c_j
 \quad\text{if }z_i=z_i'\text{ for every }i\ne j.
\]
\end{lemma}

statements.label: lem:four:edge-isolator
statements.title: Isolating one edge by signed cycle weights
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{lemma}[Isolating one edge by signed cycle weights]
\label{lem:four:edge-isolator}
Let $r\ge3$ and $\alpha>0$. There exists $m_0=m_0(r,\alpha)$ such that
the following holds for every integer $m\ge m_0$.
Let $B$ be a graph on $m$ vertices with
$\delta(B)\ge(\delta_{C_r}+\alpha)m$, and let $e\in E(B)$.
Then there is $I_{B,e}:\mathcal C_r(B)\to\mathbb R$ such that
\[
\sum_{C\ni f}I_{B,e}(C)=\ind_{\{f=e\}}\quad(f\in E(B)),\qquad
|I_{B,e}(C)|\le1\quad(C\in\mathcal C_r(B)),
\]
and
\[
\sum_{C\ni v}I_{B,e}(C)=\tfrac12\ind_{\{v\in e\}}\quad(v\in V(B)).
\]
\end{lemma}

statements.label: thm:pr:ordinary-wheel-weights
statements.title: Positive ordinary wheel weights
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Positive ordinary wheel weights]
\label{thm:pr:ordinary-wheel-weights}
Fix $r\ge3$, $\vartheta\ge\max\{1/2,\delta_{C_r}\}$,
$\alpha,\gamma,b_-,b_+>0$, and an integer $k\ge\max\{r+2,m_0(r,\alpha/4)\}$,
where $m_0$ is from Lemma~\ref{lem:four:edge-isolator}.
There exist $\eta_0>0$ and $n_0\in\mathbb N$ such that the following
holds for $n\ge n_0$. Let $V,U$ be disjoint sets with $|V|=n$, $|U|\le n$,
and let $P,\mathcal F$ be graphs
on $V$, and let $Q\subseteq P^{\rm adm}:=P-E(\mathcal F)$ and $H\subseteq V\times U$.

Let $\mathcal S(xy,u),\mathcal T(v,u,u')$ be the families of
\eqref{eq:ordinary:isolator-sets} and Section~\ref{sec:ordinary:transfer-configurations}. Assume
\[
 d_Q(v)=2d_H(v),\qquad d_H(v)\ge\gamma n\quad(v\in V),
\]
\[
 \sum_{u\in N_H(x)\cap N_H(y)}|\mathcal S(xy,u)|
       \ge\gamma n^{k-1}\quad(xy\in E(Q)),
\]
\begin{equation}
 |\mathcal T(v,u,u')|\ge\gamma n^{r^2}
 \quad(v\in V,\ u\ne u'\in N_H(v)).
 \label{eq:family:OF.A22}
\end{equation}

Let $0\le\eta\le\eta_0$, put
$\mathcal W=\{(C,u)\in\mathcal W_r^{\rm ord}((V,U,Q,H)):
 E(\mathcal F[V(C)])=\varnothing\}$, and let
$\omega_0:\mathcal W\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ satisfy
\[
b_-n^{1-r}\le\omega_0(W)\le b_+n^{1-r},\qquad
\left|\sum_{W\ni e}\omega_0(W)-1\right|\le\eta
\quad(e\in E(Q)\dot\cup E(H)).
\]

Then there is $\omega:\mathcal W\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ with
\[
\sum_{W\ni e}\omega(W)=1\quad(e\in E(Q)\dot\cup E(H)),\qquad
\tfrac{b_-}2n^{1-r}\le\omega(W)\le(b_++b_-/2)n^{1-r}\quad(W\in\mathcal W).
\]
\end{theorem}

statements.label: def:marked:common-paths
statements.title: Marked cycle and common-path families
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Marked cycle and common-path families]
\label{def:marked:common-paths}
Let $c\ge8$ and $b\ge0$ be integers. Let $V,W$ be disjoint finite sets,
$\pi$ a permutation of $V$, and $\mathcal Q=(R^0,R^K,H^0,H^K)$,
where $R^0,R^K$ are digraphs on $V$ and $H^0,H^K$ are edge-disjoint
bipartite graphs on $(V,W)$. Put $R=R^0\dot\cup R^K$ and
$H=H^0\dot\cup H^K$. Use the physical image map
$\operatorname{phys}$ of \eqref{eq:physical:image-map}: an arc $x\to y$ has image $\{x,y\}$
in type $0$ and $\{x,\pi(y)\}$ in type $K$; a spoke $vu$ has image
$\{v,u\}$. Put $\mathcal W(\mathcal Q)=\mathcal W_c^K(\mathcal Q;b,\pi)$.

Let $\mathcal C_R$ consist of the directed $c$-cycles $C$ in $R$ with
one type-$K$ arc, a $(b,\pi)$-separated vertex set, $|\operatorname{phys}(E(C))|=c$
and $|\operatorname{phys}(e)|=2$ for every $e\in E(C)$. Put
\[
 W_C=\{u\in W:W(C,u)\in\mathcal W(\mathcal Q)\},\qquad
 \mathcal C(u,u')=\{C\in\mathcal C_R:u,u'\in W_C\}\quad(u\ne u'\in W).
\]
For any typed marked $c$-cycle $C$ on labels in $V$, put $t_C(v)=K$
at its marked head and $0$ elsewhere.

For $j\in\{0,K\}$, $v\in V$ and an ordered tuple
$\mathbf z=(z_1,\ldots,z_{c-1})$ of distinct labels in $V\setminus\{v\}$,
let $C_j(v,\mathbf z)$ be $vz_1\cdots z_{c-1}v$, with unique type-$K$
arc $z_{c-1}\to v$ when $j=K$, and $z_2\to z_3$ when $j=0$.
For distinct $v,v'\in V$ and $u,u'\in W$, let
$\mathcal F_j(v,v';u,u')$ consist of the tuples $\mathbf z$ below.
For each tuple put $C_1=C_j(v,\mathbf z)$ and $C_2=C_j(v',\mathbf z)$;
the defining conditions are:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item\label{item:common-path:arcs} the labels avoid $v,v'$, and both $C_j(v,\mathbf z)$ and
$C_j(v',\mathbf z)$ have their prescribed typed arcs in $R$;
\item\label{item:common-path:spokes} $z_i u,z_i u'\in E(H^{t_{C_j(v,\mathbf z)}(z_i)})$ for every $i$;
\item\label{item:common-path:separation} $\operatorname{dist}_\pi(z_i,z_k)>b$ for $i\ne k$, and
$\operatorname{dist}_\pi(z_i,v),\operatorname{dist}_\pi(z_i,v')>b$ for every $i$;
\item\label{item:common-path:physical} $|\operatorname{phys}(E(C_\ell))|=c$ and $|\operatorname{phys}(e)|=2$ for
$\ell\in\{1,2\}$, $e\in E(C_\ell)$; moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{phys}(e)=\operatorname{phys}(f)\ \Longrightarrow\
 (\operatorname{tail}(e),\operatorname{type}(e))
 =(\operatorname{tail}(f),\operatorname{type}(f))
 \quad(e\in E(C_1),\ f\in E(C_2)).
\]
\end{enumerate}
The four root spokes $vu,vu',v'u,v'u'$ are not required to be present;
no separation between $v$ and $v'$ is imposed.
We call $W_C$ the compatible hub set of $C$, $\mathcal C(u,u')$
the common marked-cycle family at $u,u'$, and $\mathcal F_j(v,v';u,u')$
the common marked-path family with roots $v,v';u,u'$ and root type $j$.
All three use separation $(b,\pi)$.
\end{definition}

statements.label: def:marked:wheel-estimates
statements.title: Marked host estimates
statements.statement_tex:
\begin{definition}[Marked host estimates]
\label{def:marked:wheel-estimates}
Let $V,W$ be disjoint nonempty sets, $|V|=n$, and let $\pi$ be a permutation of $V$.
Let $\mathcal Q=(R^0,R^K,H^0,H^K)$, where the rim graphs are digraphs
on $V$ and the spoke graphs are edge-disjoint bipartite graphs on $(V,W)$.
Put $R=R^0\dot\cup R^K$ and $H=H^0\dot\cup H^K$.
Fix integers $c\ge8$, $b\ge1$, $D_{\rm exc}\ge0$, and reals $D,p>0$,
and spoke targets $\varsigma_0,\varsigma_K\in(0,1]$.
Use the $(b,\pi)$-separated families $\mathcal C_R$, $W_C$,
$\mathcal C(u,u')$ and $\mathcal F_j(v,v';u,u')$.

We say that $(\mathcal Q,(\varsigma_j))$ has
\emph{$(b,\pi)$-separated marked host estimates} at degree $D$ and rim density $p$,
with errors $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ and extension coefficient $\beta$,
rim bounds $(\tau,\delta_{\rm cut},h)$ and exception bound $D_{\rm exc}$,
if the following hold. Here the errors are nonnegative, the lower bounds
are positive and $0<\delta_{\rm cut}<1/4$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(MH\arabic*)}]
\item\label{item:mw:rim} \emph{Rim degrees and cuts.}
\[
\begin{gathered}
 |d^\pm_{R^0}(v)-pD|\le\varepsilon n,\qquad
 |d^\pm_{R^K}(v)-pD/(c-1)|\le\varepsilon n\quad(v\in V),\\
 |N^+_{R^0}(x)\cap N^-_{R^0}(y)|\ge\tau n\quad(x\ne y\in V).
\end{gathered}
\]
The graph $D_{R^0}$ satisfies the $(\delta_{\rm cut},h)$ large-cut
condition \eqref{eq:cuts:large}.
\item\label{item:mw:extensions} \emph{Compatible hubs, common cycles and common paths.}
\[
 |W_C|\ge\beta n\quad(C\in\mathcal C_R),\qquad
 |\mathcal C(u,u')|\ge\beta n^c\quad(u\ne u'\in W).
\]
For $j\in\{0,K\}$, distinct $v,v'\in V$ and distinct $u,u'\in W$,
\[
 vu,vu',v'u,v'u'\in E(H^j)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 |\mathcal F_j(v,v';u,u')|\ge\beta n^{c-1}.
\]
\item\label{item:mw:spokes} \emph{Spoke intersections.}
For $j\in\{0,K\}$ and $S\subseteq W$ with $1\le|S|\le3$,
\[
 \left|\left|\bigcap_{u\in S}N_{H^j}(u)\right|
            -\varsigma_j^{|S|}n\right|\le\delta n.
\]
For every $j\in\{0,K\}$ and $x\in V$ there is
$E_x^j\subseteq V$, $|E_x^j|\le D_{\rm exc}$,
such that
\[
 \bigl||N_{H^j}(x)\cap N_{H^j}(y)|-\varsigma_j^2|W|\bigr|
 \le\delta\varsigma_j^2|W|\quad(y\in V\setminus E_x^j).
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}
